reasons: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (USD 25,000/day for 'any delay in providing a dependency'), which is directionally wrong under rule LD and fails even the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at 3 months' fees); an uncapped daily penalty triggered by any delay is walk-away territory, so 'deviation' is correctly claimed.

The redline reaches the preferred position by removing Customer-payable LDs and substituting an equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as Vendor's sole remedy — a substantively favorable and workable replacement rather than a bare deletion that would leave the delay unaddressed.

The failed minimal-edit check (0.811 changed-character ratio) is expected here: the rule requires deleting/replacing the entire LD obligation, so a whole-clause rewrite is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required [Playbook] prefix, explains what changed and why, and correctly states the disproportionality rationale without lecturing; the rationale also notes the 3-month fallback if Vendor insists on a monetary construct.
